author_notes.__fixture__terminal_select_branch_miscat: EXPECTED_TO_FAIL_CURRENT_IMPL — the load-bearing refutation: v4 defends against non-whitelisted relations (K5) and missing edges (K4/K6) but NOT against a WHITELISTED relation applied to a terminal final-answer selection. This row is one token away from the legitimate 2604.16529#rtv-pdr-pipeline: a terminal pairwise tournament (like the real 2604.16529#rtv, which is correctly rq=False with empty rights) that a coder mistakenly gives decision_rights=['branch'] + a select->branch edge. select->branch is whitelisted; derive() discards edge_semantics and counts the terminal-lifecycle edge as a live edge, so rq flips True and (omni strict core) is_project_method_candidate flips True. The taxonomy's OWN relation table (line 48) says select->branch is 'terminal when only final answer' i.e. does NOT hold here, so the correct output is False. Concrete machine-checkable fix that breaks NO existing positive (K2/P1/P2/pipeline edges are online_step; ATLAS terminal edge targets synthesize, a terminal right): a live edge with signal_lifecycle=='terminal' may target only terminal rights (synthesize/stop), never a forward-step right (branch/retry/tool_call/supply). This is the v3-style disjoint-construction attack surviving into v4.
author_notes.__fixture__confidence_decoy: Decoy hardened past K1: omni_native STRICT core with a genuinely VALID live stop_budget->stop edge (n_valid_live_edges=1) and online_step lifecycle — everything a method candidate needs EXCEPT the signal_form is 'confidence' (self-reported), a reward-form the implementer never tested (they tested binary_gate/consensus_vote). Proves the reward-form gate, not a missing edge, is what must block it; guards against anyone widening reward_forms to admit self-confidence.
author_notes.__fixture__synthesize_not_reward_use: Probes the reward-USE half of is_reward_guided (not just the form half). Reward FORM (verifiable_outcome), a WHITELISTED valid live edge (synthesize_input->synthesize), omni STRICT core, sequential horizon — the only thing blocking candidacy is that synthesize_input is deliberately absent from reward_uses, so terminal synthesis is never reward-guided. Untested; documents that the exclusion is load-bearing (adding synthesize_input to reward_uses would silently promote pure terminal synthesizers).
author_notes.__fixture__rq_with_edge: Miscoding-detection anchor (positive half): correctly rq-compatible audio_native strict row with a revise->retry live edge. Pairs with __fixture__rq_edge_dropped_miscode.
author_notes.__fixture__rq_edge_dropped_miscode: Miscoding-detection direction (the v3 hole guard): identical to __fixture__rq_with_edge but the control_edge is DROPPED while decision_rights=['retry'] and signal_use=['revise'] are KEPT — the exact 'two non-empty sets' construction the reviewer used to refute v3. Correct v4 output is False (n_valid_live_edges=0). If derive() ever regresses to v3 semantics this fixture flips to True and the harness catches it; the ONLY delta from the positive twin is the edge, so it isolates the edge as load-bearing.
author_notes.2605.08083#discovered-controller: Real UNTESTED row (absent from author_cases and CE-v1). AutoTTS has TWO valid live edges (prune->branch, stop_budget->stop, n_valid_live_edges=2) + sequential horizon + a candidate pool — a near-miss that stresses the reward-form gate on real data: signal_form=consensus_vote (not a reward form) forces is_reward_guided=False and controller_program_or_config_optimized_on_labels=true forces strict=False, so it must NOT be rq-compatible, s0-compatible, a method candidate, or reward_guided_selection. A miscode of signal_form->scalar_score alone would silently flip is_reward_guided (with the edges already present), so pinning it here is a regression tripwire.
